strings.name: Vladimir Putin
strings.role: Russian politician · Governance and international relations
strings.summary: Putin moved from Soviet intelligence into local and central administration, becoming Russian prime minister and acting president in 1999. He subsequently served multiple terms as president and prime minister and is a central figure in contemporary Russia. Relations between Russia and the West changed profoundly during his leadership. The annexation of Crimea in 2014 and the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 drew international condemnation and reshaped European security.
strings.coverageNote: Selected milestones from 1952 to 2023. The war and international legal proceedings continue to develop; these entries do not represent subsequent case status. Regional tags reflect Russia’s transcontinental associations.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-01.value: Leningrad, Soviet Union, now Saint Petersburg, Russia

strings.facts.fact-03.label: Early career

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Long-standing role in Russian leadership
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: First elected president in 2000, became prime minister in 2008 and returned to the presidency in 2012.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Impact on European security
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine under his leadership in 2022; the UN General Assembly demanded an end to the invasion and withdrawal.
strings.highlights.highlight-03.title: International legal proceedings
strings.highlights.highlight-03.text: In 2023, the International Criminal Court issued a warrant for his arrest over alleged war crimes involving the unlawful transfer of Ukrainian children. An arrest warrant is not a conviction.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: ICC issues an arrest warrant
strings.timeline.event-01.text: The International Criminal Court issued a warrant over alleged war crimes involving the unlawful transfer of children from occupied areas of Ukraine to Russia.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Russia launches its full-scale invasion of Ukraine
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Russia began a large-scale invasion. The UN General Assembly subsequently adopted a resolution demanding an end to the invasion and unconditional withdrawal.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Annexation of Crimea
strings.timeline.event-03.text: Signed legislation incorporating Crimea into Russia. A UN General Assembly resolution reaffirmed Ukraine’s territorial integrity and rejected the validity of the related referendum.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Elected Russian president again
strings.timeline.event-04.text: After four years as prime minister, won another presidential election and began a new presidential term.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Becomes Russian prime minister
strings.timeline.event-05.text: After two presidential terms, became prime minister, dividing leadership responsibilities with then-president Dmitry Medvedev.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Formally takes office as president for the first time
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Inaugurated after winning the election in March of that year; re-elected in 2004.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: From prime minister to acting president
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Became prime minister in August, then acting president after Boris Yeltsin resigned on 31 December.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Becomes director of the Federal Security Service
strings.timeline.event-08.text: After working in the presidential administration, became FSB director and additionally served as Security Council secretary the following year.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Graduates and enters intelligence work
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Graduated from Leningrad State University’s law faculty and joined the KGB, serving for a period in East Germany.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Leningrad
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Leningrad in the Soviet Union, now Saint Petersburg in Russia.
